en.title: Adjectives made from other words
en.summary: Many adjectives are built from nouns and verbs by adding an ending.

paragraphs: English makes many adjectives from other words by adding a suffix. The suffix often shows the meaning. For example -less means without, and -ful means full of. Knowing the endings helps you guess the meaning of new words.

The common endings are -y, -ful, -less, -able, -ous, -al, -ish and -ic. The -ing and -ed forms of verbs also work as adjectives. The -ing form describes the thing that causes a feeling. The -ed form describes the person who has the feeling.

A final e is dropped before -able and -ous: love becomes lovable, fame becomes famous. A final y changes to i before -ful: beauty becomes beautiful. A single consonant is doubled in fun, funny and sun, sunny.
A film is boring, but the people watching it are bored. A job is tiring, but you are tired. Choose -ing for the cause and -ed for the person who feels it.

items: Wrong: **I am very boring today.** Right: **I am very bored today.**
Wrong: **a carefull driver** Right: **a careful driver**
Wrong: **a helpfull friend** Right: **a helpful friend**

ro.title: Adjective formate din alte cuvinte
ro.summary: În limba română, multe adjective se formează din substantive sau verbe prin adăugarea unor sufixe specifice.

paragraphs: În limba română, putem crea adjective din alte cuvinte. Multe adjective se formează din substantive sau din verbe. Adăugăm la sfârșitul cuvântului grupuri speciale de litere, numite sufixe.

Sufixele se adaugă la sfârșitul unui substantiv sau al unui verb. Cele mai comune sufixe sunt -os, -esc, -ic și -tor. De asemenea, participiul unui verb poate funcționa direct ca adjectiv. Noul adjectiv se acordă în gen și număr cu substantivul.
